definitions.explanation: A coniferous tree native to Japan, valued for its fragrant, durable wood used in traditional architecture and bathtubs.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{檜|ひのき}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{建|た}てられている→建てる：01189_tateru⟧。
examples.english: This shrine is built with hinoki cypress.
Hinoki cypress baths have a nice fragrance.

examples.japanese: {檜|ひのき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦リラックス→リラックス：02531_rirakkusu⟧⟦{効果|こうか}→効果：02726_kouka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: The scent of hinoki has a relaxing effect.

notes:
Japanese cypress (Chamaecyparis obtusa).

WRITING: Also written {桧|ひのき}, and ヒノキ in botany and on labels.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {檜|ひのき}{風呂|ぶろ} (hinoki bathtub; a luxury feature of ryokan)
- {檜|ひのき}⟦{舞台|ぶたい}→舞台：03606_butai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (literally "to stand on a hinoki stage": to have one's moment in the spotlight)
- {檜|ひのき}{造|づく}り (built of hinoki)

CULTURAL NOTE: One of the finest building woods in Japan, prized for its durability, resistance to rot and fragrance. It is used for shrines (including Ise Grand Shrine), temples and traditional houses. Trees are counted with {本|ほん}.
